highlights.title: Dell’s newest laptop sounds a lot like a MacBook Neo
highlights.summary: Dell's new Dell 14S laptop sounds a lot like a MacBook Neo: it comes in four colors, is aimed at students, and it starts with 8GB of RAM and 256GB of storage. Announced at IFA 2026, the 14S is meant to sit below the recently launched XPS 13 and offer another affordable laptop option as most other…
body: The Dell 14S promises an aluminum build, Intel Wildcat Lake chips, and lots of battery life — for a price we don’t know exactly yet.

The Dell 14S isn’t as thin or as light as the XPS 13, but in addition to the same two USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 ports with DisplayPort and Power Delivery, it also has HDMI 1.4 and a 3.5mm audio jack. (Why the XPS 13 lacks a headphone jack, I’ll never understand). But the 14S has much more basic, non-touch display options: a 300-nit 1920 x 1200 / 60Hz LCD or a 450-nit 2880 x 1800 / 120Hz one.

There are some other niceties for students on the 14S, including a 1080p webcam with Windows Hello face unlock support, and battery life that Dell claims can last for up to 23 hours of Netflix streaming. For chip offerings, it’ll be either the Intel Core 5 320 or Core 7 350 — the 14S won’t scale up to Intel Panther Lake options like the XPS 13 is soon expected to.

body: Kimi Antonelli leads his Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the standings, with McLaren's Lando Norris 83 points back in fourth after belatedly igniting his title defence with victories at the last two races.
With 11 rounds remaining, Hamilton is 28 points clear of his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, while Norris has moved 55 points ahead of his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri.

Given the significant margins by which the British duo each trail Antonelli, it has been a topic of speculation as to whether either Ferrari or McLaren would consider implementing team orders sooner rather than later to aid their better-positioned driver in the title fight.

highlights.title: Google needs Hollywood more than the studios need AI
highlights.summary: Google has reportedly been reaching out to a number of Hollywood's biggest studios, hoping to strike licensing agreements that would allow it to train its AI models on copyrighted material in exchange for massive piles of cash.
body: Striking deals with studios like Disney could help the tech giant shift the narrative about artificial intelligence.

Regardless of whether a studio were to incorporate AI tools into their production workflows or simply feature user-generated AI content on their platforms (which was Disney and OpenAI’s plan before their partnership collapsed ), striking a licensing agreement with Google would be a watershed moment.

Though Google has everything to gain from Hollywood embracing AI, the studios have to be mindful of how endorsing this technology could leave them out on a limb. And as much as Google might be presenting its products as the solution to all of the entertainment industry’s issues, the AI industry needs Hollywood more than Hollywood needs more slop.

highlights.title: 28 Years Later, This Remains the Most Near-Perfect WWII Movie of All Time
highlights.summary: War movies are a genre that will never go out of style. Beyond the action they show on screen, they are also used in exploring the human condition and how it is affected by violence. War — real or fictional — is never an easy thing, especially for those involved on the frontlines.
body: Recently, we covered the 10 best films about WWII, but there is one film in particular that stands out thanks to director Steven Spielberg's unflinching look at the invasion of Normandy.

Largely considered one of the great war movies ever made, Saving Private Ryan has made a home in the hearts of many, where it continues to resonate even 28 years on. The film is inspired by the real-life events of Sergeant Frederick Niland and follows a group of U.S. soldiers as they work to rescue paratrooper Private Ryan (Matt Damon), the sole survivor of his brothers after three were killed in action, and send him home.

Spielberg's attention to detail provides the action, but it is his storytelling that sets Saving Private Ryan apart from the rest. Rather than focusing solely on war itself, the film chooses to focus instead on the humans who must trudge through it. Their mission, as ordered by their superiors, is to locate and bring Private Ryan home — a task that forces the squad to risk their lives within a theater of war.
points: War movies are a genre that will never go out of style.
Beyond the action they show on screen, they are also used in exploring the human condition and how it is affected by violence.

highlights.title: Whisky galore – and now plenty more besides: exploring the Scottish island of Islay
highlights.summary: Distilleries are the backbone of Islay’s economy and tourist trade. Thanks to their success, other businesses – from breweries and farms to restaurants and chocolatiers – are now thriving and adding to the island’s appeal.
body: The Paps of Jura disappear into the mist as I pedal along the shores of Loch Indaal, and the rain cloud I’ve been racing finally catches up. I stash my hire bike at Port Charlotte youth hostel, quickly change and make it to Lochindaal Seafood Kitchen just before the downpour.

I’m soon warmed, by the welcome then by a bowl of creamy fish chowder. “We’ve plenty of fresh seafood just in,” is all the temptation I need to order the seafood plate. It’s a bowl for one, but a hungry one, and soon I’m picking and cracking my way through piles of fat langoustines and crab claws, with hot whisky-butter scallops and plenty of bread and butter.

The island of Islay, off the west coast of Scotland, is far better known for its drinks than its food. With 10, soon to be 11, working whisky distilleries, Islay is synonymous with rich, heavily peated single malts. But, over several days cycling around the island, I find that whisky does much more than fill warehouses and attract tourists. It is helping to support an island where agriculture, fishing and hospitality have long struggled to provide year-round employment.

body: Along with the announcement, a slew of early impressions popped up, including from Every CEO Dan Shipper, who claims, “It’s the strongest coding model we’ve used, but now it’s fast, token-efficient, and crucially actually speaks like a normal person.”

Box CEO Aaron Levie is another early access believer, saying that his company’s agent with Fable 5.1 picked up on subtleties and ambiguities in data that Fable 5 missed in the same test. Meanwhile, Lisan al Gaib points out that on benchmarks, Mythos 5.1 with low reasoning scores the same as its predecessor set to Max reasoning.

Fable 5.1 also has “more precise safeguards” that Anthropic says are less likely to block basic biology questions than Fable 5, but Mythos 5.1 has the same biology restrictions as the previous model. Anthropic also explained its progress on data retention, saying that Enterprise Frontier Safeguards offer “complete privacy” by storing data on the customer’s cloud servers instead of its own, and will start rolling out later this fall.

highlights.title: LEGO Star Wars: The Mandalorian Review
highlights.summary: LEGO Star Wars: The Mandalorian is a goofy and fun tribute to the live-action series, but it’s hard not to wish that this animated special told a completely original story. Read our full review.
body: At this point, it’s anyone’s guess as to whether or not we’ll ever see The Mandalorian Season 4 on Disney+. The tepid response to The Mandalorian and Grogu in theaters shows that this branch of the Star Wars franchise doesn’t carry the same weight it once did. It’s entirely possible that LEGO Star Wars: The Mandalorian is the last hurrah for this particular series, with Din Djarin and his little buddy relegated to appearing in Dave Filoni’s Mando-verse crossover movie. If so, fans are left with a fun but ultimately forgettable tribute to a show that was once the bright center of the Star Wars universe.

LEGO Star Wars: The Mandalorian is essentially a tribute to/recap of all three seasons of the live-action series, along with The Book of Boba Fett for good measure. There’s some new material here in the form of a framing device involving Mando’s friends throwing him a party, but for the most part, this animated special focuses on having various characters recount Din (Gavin Hammon) and Grogu’s (David Acord) exploits with a suitably goofy LEGO flourish.

highlights.title: ‘The Indies’ Goes on a Journey With 3 Men Taking a Painting Across a Europe Ravaged by Conflicts (Exclusive Venice Trailer)
highlights.summary: The period road movie, the debut fiction feature from Pauline Julier and Nicolas Chapoulier, premieres in the Venice Days program, using a historical lens to examine the origins of the world we inhabit today.
body: In 1652, Spanish artist Diego Velázquez painted the portrait of Maria Theresa of Austria, Infanta of Spain. “Infanta” was a royal title given to the daughters of a monarch who were not the direct heir to the throne. A few weeks later, the painting reached the court of Louis XIV, who was still a child, sealing the union of the French and Spanish monarchies, as well as peace after the Thirty Years’ War.

“In our own time, when images circulate instantaneously, imagining the creation and transport of this painting, and its political significance, struck us as a powerful dramatic engine,” the co-directors share in a directors’ note. “It is the 17th century: the medieval era is fading in the face of the rise of science, rationalism, and commerce. The world is no longer merely to be explored – it is to be conquered.”

highlights.title: A moment that changed me: I had a panic attack on public transport – and it led me to a horrifying secret
highlights.summary: For a decade I lived with a fear so bad that I once tried to climb out of a tube carriage while it was in motion. Then a hypnotherapist told me to ask my parents one very important question. In 2000, I had been living in London for just over a decade and working at EMI Records for five years.
body: As things got progressively worse, I had a string of distressing panic attacks. Every time, it felt like the world around me was closing in. Then, in July 2003, during my daily commute between Brixton and the South Bank, I had a panic attack so intense I tried to climb out of the tube carriage doors. Thankfully, other passengers held me back until we arrived at the next platform – but I knew the problem was no longer something I could ignore.

The following year, my GP referred me to a hypnotherapist. During regression hypnotherapy sessions, I would sit on a chair, close my eyes and feel as if I was falling back through time to different points in my life. After three months of retracing old memories, my therapist asked me plainly if I had ever been in a train crash. “No, I think I’d know if I’d been in a train crash,” I said, slightly taken aback. Despite my insistence, she asked if I would double-check with my parents next time I saw them, in case I had been too young to remember.

highlights.title: Walter Torous named executive director of MIT Center for Real Estate
highlights.summary: The senior lecturer, already director of the degree program, will now oversee all aspects of the center’s activities and operations.
body: Walter Torous, senior lecturer in the MIT Department of Urban Studies and Planning (DUSP) and the MIT Sloan School of Management, and director of the Master of Science in Real Estate Development Program (MSRED), was recently named executive director of the MIT Center for Real Estate (CRE) — effective July 1, 2026.

In announcing Torous’ appointment, School of Architecture and Planning Dean Hashim Sarkis also said that Justin Steil, professor of law and urban planning, will represent CRE as faculty chair of the Academic Curriculum Council.

“Together, Walter and Justin will guide CRE’s academic and strategic direction as it continues to strengthen its role within our school and the Institute,” Sarkis said. “Their appointments reflect the center’s distinctive position at the intersection of finance, design, planning, technology, and public policy — and its long-standing commitment to understanding real estate not only as a market force, but also as a driver of urban transformation and social change.”

highlights.summary: Everton's move for Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has fallen through following a change of heart from the player after the deal scuppered Chelsea's chances of signing Lamine Camara.
body: Balogun arrived in Merseyside at lunchtime to complete the £40m Deadline Day transfer, but doubts began to emerge that the deal would be completed after an issue came up in the medical.
As a result, Monaco moved to sell midfielder Camara instead, but in another twist, Everton renegotiated Balogun's deal to force the move through.
Despite having a full agreement to sell Camara to Chelsea in place, Monaco withdrew from the deal as the 11pm transfer deadline passed, which left the Blues furious.
Chelsea also had the chance to withdraw from the £125m move to sell Enzo Fernandez to Man City, but chose not to out of good faith.

highlights.title: Supercell’s acquisition of Merge Mansion maker Metacore to be finalised this month
highlights.summary: Metacore has officially signed an agreement with Supercell that means Merge Mansion and its team will become part of the Finnish firm at the end of this month. Financial terms have not been disclosed.
body: The two companies announced the acquisition in a joint announcement earlier this year, revealing that integration planning was already underway. Metacore closed its offices in Germany and Sweden and cut 159 staff at its Helsinki HQ as part of the move.

“Merge Mansion created a completely new genre and has all the ingredients of a game that can be played for years and remembered forever,” said Supercell president Sara Bach. “We believe in what this game can become, and really look forward to welcoming the Merge Mansion team to Supercell and working together on the game’s next chapter.”

Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski added that the team is “excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team, and our players,” and stressed that player experience remains the priority as the game changes hands.

Merge Mansion, credited with kickstarting the merge genre on mobile, retains a loyal player base. According to AppMagic estimates, the merge puzzler has generated around $7.7m in the last 30 days alone, and is thought to have earned around $540m since its 2020 launch.

Add the chicken thighs, give them a good mix to coat, then pop them in the fridge to marinate for at least an hour.

Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan)/390F/gas 6. Meanwhile, put a glug of olive oil in an oven-safe saute pan on a high heat. Chuck in the onions and peppers, fry for two to three minutes, until colooured and slightly blackened, then add the garlic and fry for a minute more, until fragrant.

Turn down the heat to medium, squeeze in the tomato puree and cook for one minute, until the mix darkens. Season generously, then tip in the rice and toast for a minute. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and chicken stock, and bring to a bubble.

highlights.title: It’s not easy to show my scars. But I am proud to break the deadly silence around breast cancer in Nigeria | Gloria Chinyere Okwu
highlights.summary: I was told to keep my diagnosis private but I am determined to show the reality of breast cancer and reject the stigma that prevents women seeking treatment. ‘Madam, this looks like breast cancer, and if it is, we will chop off your breast.” That was how the doctor welcomed me into the chaotic…
body: For a moment, I could no longer hear him. I thought of my three children, the university degree I had just bagged and the future I had envisaged. If I was going to die, what was the point of it all? I had invested everything I had to obtain that degree, subjecting my children to days of absence while I spent my nights in the university library.

The biopsy result was ready in seven days and the doctor was right: the next course of action was a mastectomy. Everyone had an opinion. My mother insisted a medicine man could heal me and begged me to cancel the scheduled surgery. My friends dragged me to churches because all I needed was prayers to be healed. As the surgery drew near, their voices grew louder. I was berated for lack of faith.

I had been told that the mastectomy was the solution and, after that, I could focus on my life again. That turned out not to be entirely true. A few days after my mastectomy, a group of doctors stood by my bedside and informed me that I would need further treatment, including chemotherapy.

highlights.title: OpenAI Is About to Release Its First AI Model With ‘Critical’ Cyber Abilities
highlights.summary: The company will give select partners early access to its Astra AI model—so they have time to shore up their defenses.
body: OpenAI announced Tuesday that its forthcoming AI model, Astra, is its first to reach the company’s threshold for what it calls “critical” cyber capabilities. OpenAI says it plans to publicly release a version of Astra “soon,” but will make the model’s advanced cyber capabilities available only to select partners in its Daybreak Blue early-access program at launch.

In a briefing with reporters, OpenAI safety and security leaders said the company has concluded that Astra reaches the critical cybersecurity capabilities outlined in its preparedness framework, which sets thresholds and protocols for when its AI models pose new levels of risk. The company says an AI model has reached its critical cyber threshold when it can independently find and exploit previously unknown vulnerabilities in real-world software. OpenAI leaders said the company has followed its procedure for this situation, which is to halt further development until appropriate safeguards and security measures can be implemented.
points: The company will give select partners early access to its Astra AI model—so they have time to shore up their defenses.

highlights.title: Football connects communities but can pull them apart if governed carelessly
highlights.summary: Sport is a space to help youngsters develop character, resilience and confidence, but we need stronger leadership and safer environments to make this happen. The fight for the soul of football isn’t just happening in the offices of Uefa and Fifa, it’s taking place on pitches much closer to home.
body: This isn’t just a Scottish problem. Contacts I speak to in different roles around football confirm and almost accept that “youth football is atrocious”. This should be sounding major alarm bells, for the consequences go way beyond the pitch. The existing disciplinary systems and PR campaigns are not nearly enough to address and change the situation.

There is no shortage of evidence about how important it is – whether you are trying to develop skilful football players or healthy young people – that children need space to play, try stuff out and thrive. We also know that it’s what children want from sport. Research by Amanda Visek at the Milken Institute of Public Health at George Washington University, confirms that when it comes to organised sport, kids just want to have fun. What counts for girls and boys are things like trying your best, working hard, playing well together as a team. When mapping 81 determinants of fun, “winning” ranked 40th in importance.

The Campaign for Children’s Rights in Football is an independent and impartial organisation. It’s preparing to launch and trying to create a greater platform for its work in the sport internationally. It’s needed more than ever.

body: Consumer group Which? says it was able to create a fake listing for 10 Downing Street on travel giant Booking.com.

The UK watchdog said its researchers were able to book a bogus stay at the prime minister's address - as well as leave a fake review noting "hanging out" with resident mouser Larry the cat as a highlight.
It said despite clear signs it was fake, Booking.com did not remove the listing until two months after it was uploaded.
They said because Which?'s listing was not "live" on its site across the two months it was present, "some of our automatic fraud controls were not triggered to completely remove the closed listing".

highlights.title: The rise of AI ‘civilizations’ and the fall of corporate responsibility
highlights.summary: Depending on who you ask, developer platform Hugging Face was recently attacked by OpenAI - after it lost control of its own AI tools - or by a succession of AI "civilizations." Welcome to the linguistic battlefield of AI safety, where word choices can shift responsibility for a massive…
body: Until last week, the details surrounding the OpenAI-Hugging Face hack felt fairly settled. In July, a cybersecurity test of one of OpenAI’s autonomous AI agents went wrong. The agent escaped its supposedly isolated test environment, accessed the internet, and hacked Hugging Face, alongside several other organizations. A good deal remained unknown, and there are many serious questions left around safety and governance, but the basic shape was clear. Detailed accounts from OpenAI and two independent research groups were supposed to fill in the gaps, but when they published their reports last week, it turned out the hack was much stranger than it initially seemed.

It’s a lot to parse. Between them, the reports run to around 130 pages, much of which is both dense and highly technical. A few days later, Dwarkesh Patel, a podcaster little known outside of tech circles but with outsized reach and influence among Silicon Valley’s AI establishment, set out to tell “The whole OpenAI/Hugging Face story in plain English.” He titled his Substack blog “The Rise and Fall of Agent Civilizations.”

According to Nintendo's official patch notes, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe now supports up to eight players on a single screen on Switch 2, doubling the number of players possible in split-screen on the original Nintendo Switch. Switch 2 owners can now connect up to seven Nintendo Switch controllers — either Joy-Cons or Switch Pro Controllers — to play eight-player split-screen. body: Danny Boyle’s movie, adapted by James Graham from his own play, is a primal scene of modern Britain and its agonies over class, culture and empire. Rupert Murdoch buys the Sun newspaper in 1969 and turns it into a raucous circulation powerhouse of sexist smut and Tory politics, while gloating over the timid British establishment who winced at the colonial Australian press baron. Guy Pearce plays Murdoch and Jack O’Connell plays editor Larry Lamb.

Here is the latest episode – drawn from hundreds of hours of experimental immersive improv footage filmed in Ukraine 15 years ago – in a colossal and controversial multimedia movie project so epic and bizarre that it’s still hard to believe it actually exists. Russian director Ilya Khrzhanovsky has created a new filmic part of his massive portrait of the Soviet scientist Lev Landau (or “Dau”) and his 60s experimental psychology unit, in which he experiences sexual angst and ponders the possibility of love within a totalitarian society.

highlights.title: How Des Kohan Became LA’s Under-the-Radar Fashion Power Player
highlights.summary: Desiree Kohan’s boutique takes an anti-trend approach to fashion at a time when algorithms determine what we wear more than ever. Designers and customers are embracing the model.
body: For the last 21 years in Los Angeles, Desiree Kohan’s boutique, Des Kohan, has been a destination for fashion discovery. And this September, she will do something she hasn’t felt compelled to do in years: go to New York Fashion Week.

Kohan has never made the seasonal circuit a priority, but a group of independent female designers she believes in — Ashlynn Park of Ashlyn, Maria McManus, and Alissa Zachary of High Sport — has become increasingly important to the mix at Des Kohan. Ashlyn and McManus will show in New York, while High Sport plans to present its collection digitally.

“I feel that they’re being authentic to who they are, and they’re all three unique,” Kohan says. Their approach reminds her of advice Dries Van Noten once offered on how to grow her store slowly with loyal partners. “That’s how these designers are.”
